candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because the order service returns 502, which traces show originates from payment returning 503 on POST /v1/authorizations; the failure is a downstream server error propagated up the chain, not gateway-local.
candidates.uncertainty: Payment-side cause of the 503 (config, saturation, or dependency) is not observed; only the propagation path is established.

report.explanation: Traces show checkout 502 caused by order 502, which is caused by payment 503 on /v1/authorizations; inventory/redis succeed. Logs and metrics confirm gateway 502s on /v1/checkout with fast durations, ruling out gateway latency. Root cause lies in the payment service, which is not directly observed.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/traces for /v1/authorizations 503 root cause
Payment service metrics (error rate, saturation, dependency health)
